summary: Static review of build.cmd/build.ps1 wrapper fix for AwakeToggle Windows tray tool + pytest regression on Linux. All checks pass; 54 tests still green.

build.cmd.line_endings: CRLF (verified via `file` command: 'DOS batch file, ASCII text, with CRLF line terminators')
build.cmd.syntax: Valid batch: `@echo off` + powershell invocation + `if errorlevel 1 pause`
build.cmd.powershell_invocation: powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File "%~dp0build.ps1" — %~dp0 ensures script resolves relative to the .cmd location so it works from any cwd; -ExecutionPolicy Bypass bypasses the Zone.Identifier/unsigned-script block that caused the user's PSSecurityException
build.cmd.error_propagation: `if errorlevel 1 pause` keeps window open on failure so user sees error; note: exit code is not re-raised to caller, which is fine for a double-click/manual build but would not fail a parent script. Acceptable for the stated use case.

build.ps1.repo_root: Set-Location (Split-Path $PSScriptRoot -Parent) — correctly moves to repo root regardless of invocation cwd

README.md.selbst_bauen_section: Line 205 references `.\tools\build.cmd` with comment 'umgeht die Skript-Sperre von PowerShell' — matches the fix

critical_code_review_comments: Minor: build.cmd does not propagate exit code to caller (only pauses). If a CI wrapper ever invokes build.cmd it will not see failure. Add `exit /b %errorlevel%` after the pause for defensive propagation.

Nit: README code fence is powershell-tagged but line 205 is a .cmd invocation; still works since users just copy the command, but a short note that build.cmd can be double-clicked from Explorer would help the target audience.

success_rate.frontend: n/a (Windows desktop tool, no web frontend)
